QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_14

question.text: If a bond is trading at a premium and has a coupon rate of 9%, which of the following is true?

explanation.text: The Logic: For a premium bond, the coupon rate is the highest, current yield falls in the middle, and YTM is the lowest. Because the investor pays more than face value, the effective yield to maturity is pulled below the coupon rate, with current yield (coupon divided by price) sitting in between. The Trap: Do not reverse the premium-bond order: coupon rate is highest and YTM is lowest. The reversed inequality applies to discount bonds, and equality of all three holds only for par bonds. Note: Rewrote the trap explanation in words rather than relying on raw comparison signs that can be swallowed in rendering, and removed the cross-exam and pro-tip paragraphs.
